axiom-bokeh: Liked as a glidey, long, straight fairway driver; many find flight varies by plastic and run.
axiom-crave: Praised as a straight, accurate fairway driver that goes far; many find flight varies by plastic and run.
axiom-envy: Praised for accuracy, a comfortable grip and surprising distance; some find flight shifts with plastic.
axiom-hex: Liked as a straight, predictable midrange with a comfortable grip; some find stability varies by run.
axiom-insanity: Liked as a long, understable driver for hyzer flips and distance; many find runs fly very differently.
axiom-proxy: Praised as a very straight, predictable putter that holds lines; few real complaints.
axiom-pyro: Loved as an overstable midrange, especially forehand, with a reliable fade; some find it quick to die.
axiom-tempo: Liked as a straight, forgiving low-speed disc for forehand approaches; some find it too straight.
discraft-zone: Valued as an overstable approach disc with a dependable fade; few real complaints.
innova-destroyer: Valued for distance, forehands and headwinds; many find stability varies widely between plastics.
innova-firebird: Valued as a very overstable driver with a hard, dependable fade; some find it hooks early at low speed.
innova-fox: Liked as a very understable, glidey mid for hyzer flips and wooded lines; some find it too flippy.
innova-gorgon: Loved for easy distance from a glidey understable driver; some find copies turn over too much.
innova-leopard: Liked as a straight, forgiving fairway driver for newer players; some find runs inconsistent.
innova-mako3: Liked as a very straight, honest midrange that suits beginners; some find it turns over as it beats in.
innova-mamba: Liked for long hyzer flips and turnovers with plenty of glide; many find copies fly very differently.
innova-shryke: Praised for the longest throws, suiting open fields and forehand bombs; many find stability inconsistent.
innova-teebird3: Valued as a workhorse fairway driver with a reliable fade; some find it too overstable when new.
innova-thunderbird: Valued for a fairly straight flight and reliable fade; many find stability varies a lot between runs.
innova-toro: Liked as an overstable forehand approach disc; some find it clunky, with little glide.
innova-valkyrie: Liked as a friendly driver for developing arms with good distance; some find it beats in and turns over.
innova-wraith: Praised for distance, especially on forehand; many find copies beat in quickly and turn flippy.
kastaplast-berg: Valued as a low-glide approach and putting disc that sits where it lands; some find distance limited.
kastaplast-jarn: Liked as an overstable approach disc, best forehand; some find it has little glide and an odd rim.
latitude-64-fuse: Liked as a very straight, glidey midrange for beginners and tight lines; some find it too flippy.
latitude-64-pure: Liked as a putter for both putting and throwing, with a comfortable feel; a few want more glide.
latitude-64-river: Loved for lots of glide and easy distance, even for slower arms; some find it turns over with power.
mvp-detour: Liked as an understable midrange that flips up with good distance; some find it turns over too easily.
mvp-reactor: Praised as a slightly overstable midrange with a dependable fade, good on forehands; few real complaints.
mvp-resistor: Valued as a very overstable fairway driver for forehands and wind; many find runs inconsistent.
mvp-servo: Liked for reliable straight flights and hyzer flips; some find stability varies by plastic and run.
mvp-tesla: Liked as a hard-fading forehand driver; many find copies are meathooks, especially backhand.
mvp-trail: Liked for easy distance and glide at modest arm speeds; many find copies inconsistent and flippy.
mvp-watt: Liked as a straight, floaty putter for upshots that holds lines; few real complaints.
mvp-wave: Praised for distance on hyzer flips and turnovers; many find it often turns over.
prodigy-a2: Praised as a very overstable approach disc for forehand flex shots; some find it dumps quickly.
prodigy-a5: Rated as a straight to stable approach disc, especially forehand; some find stability varies by plastic.
streamline-range: Liked as a glidey approach and putting disc that holds lines; some find it turns over when thrown hard.
streamline-trace: Liked as a long, straight driver that works forehand; some find it too flippy, especially lighter copies.
westside-harp: Valued as a very overstable approach disc with a reliable fade; some find it has little glide.
